solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Chap’s tax-free savings account

blocks.note: an ISA, an Individual Savings Account, is the UK's tax-free savings scheme
AC is the standard abbreviation for account

explanation.surface: Someone describes a man's personal tax-free savings account.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one phrase, a chap's ISA, but it splits into a tax-free savings product and its account abbreviation, with the definition at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Crosswords use 'chap' for any male first name, and Isaac is one such given name.

clue.text: Just like one mimicking, say, Renoir in cinema early on

definitions.text: Just like one mimicking, say, Renoir in cinema early on

indicators.note: what comes early on in a phrase is at its start, so only the opening letters are taken

blocks.note: an impressionist mimics people, and Renoir was an Impressionist painter: both readings land on one word
the first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: An actor in an early film does an impersonation of the painter Renoir.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: being just like an impressionist is to be impressionistic. 'Say' marks Renoir as one example of an Impressionist painter.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes work in the manner of the Impressionist painters, or anything resembling such loose, suggestive treatment.

clue.text: Nothing being in touch is concerning

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: the letter O looks like zero, or nothing
to abut is to touch along a border

explanation.surface: Someone claims that keeping in touch with nobody is worrying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In touch' looks like one phrase, but 'in' belongs to the container signal and 'touch' alone is the verb that supplies the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words work as prepositions meaning on the subject of, as in a book about or concerning birds.

clue.text: Crimea suffering being invaded by hard monster

indicators.note: something suffering is in a bad way, damaged, so its letters are knocked out of shape
a country invaded by an army has that army inside its borders

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A news line about the suffering of Crimea under invasion by some brutal monster.
explanation.walkthrough: The geopolitical surface hides two mechanics: the place name is the anagram fodder, and the hard letter is slipped inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Chimera was a fire-breathing beast with lion, goat and serpent parts, a classic monster.

clue.text: Presentation speech is holding record

indicators.note: whatever is holding something wraps around it and keeps it inside

blocks.note: diction is one's manner of speaking
an EP, extended play, is a kind of record

explanation.surface: An awards-night presentation speech that clings on to some record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Presentation speech' reads as one thing; the first word is the definition and 'speech' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A depiction is a portrayal or representation of something, which is one sense of a presentation of it.

clue.text: One’s leaving perfect bargain

indicators.note: 'one is leaving' says a letter departs from the word that follows

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
ideal means perfect

explanation.surface: Someone's departure is described as a perfect bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the I that 'One' supplies from IDEAL to leave DEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A deal is an agreement or transaction, and a good bargain is often called a deal.

clue.text: Possibly flat pastry mistake over putting fruit in

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned over means flipped upside down so it reads backwards
putting one thing in places it inside the other

blocks.note: a pie is a pastry dish
to err is to make a mistake
a date is a fruit of the palm

explanation.surface: A baking disaster: the pastry has gone flat, perhaps because the fruit was put in wrongly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' looks like a description of failed pastry; it is the noun for a small home. 'Possibly' marks the definition as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A pied-à-terre is a small second residence kept in a city, often an apartment, which Britons call a flat.

clue.text: Mike invested in fuel — that’s ridiculous

indicators.note: money invested in a business is put inside it

blocks.note: mike and mic are both short forms of microphone
coal is a fuel

explanation.surface: Someone named Mike put money into a fuel company, and a friend calls it absurd.
explanation.walkthrough: Mike looks like the NATO alphabet's M, but here it is the informal word for a microphone.
explanation.definitionFit: Something comical provokes laughter, much as something ridiculous invites mockery; the two are close synonyms.

clue.text: One new exam in English of which colon is a part

definitions.text: of which colon is a part

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
N is the abbreviation for new
a test is an exam
taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A new English exam that tests punctuation, including the colon.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon in the surface is a punctuation mark sitting in an English paper; in the definition it is the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: The colon is the main section of the large bowel, so it is one part of the digestive tube named here.

clue.text: In spite of being without status

blocks.note: without means not with
standing is one's status or reputation

explanation.surface: A remark about someone carrying on despite having no social standing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' is read literally as two words, and the answer breaks into three plain words.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a formal preposition meaning despite, as in 'notwithstanding the rain, we went out'.

clue.text: Closest human perhaps circling bull?

indicators.note: to circle something is to go round it on all sides

blocks.note: humans are one kind of primate; 'perhaps' marks an example
an ox is a bovine animal, though strictly a castrated one, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: A person nearest the ring, perhaps, circling round a bull at a bullfight.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that an ox is not quite a bull, since it is usually castrated.
explanation.definitionFit: Proximate means nearest or immediately next, as in a proximate cause, so it matches a superlative of nearness.

clue.text: Choral piece assembled around Biblical texts

indicators.note: around means on every side of, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: people who assembled met together
OT is the Old Testament, a body of Biblical texts

explanation.surface: A piece for choir built up from verses of scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Assembled' looks like putting the music together; it is the gathering of people, past tense.
explanation.definitionFit: A motet is a short polyphonic sacred composition for voices, a typical item sung by a church choir.

clue.text: One of two I encountered in upper atmosphere

indicators.note: something encountered in a place is found inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
the ether is an old word for the clear upper sky

explanation.surface: Someone claims to have met one of a pair high up in the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: The ether, in older poetic usage, was the rarefied air above the clouds.
explanation.definitionFit: Either picks out one or the other of a pair, as in 'either road will do'.

clue.text: Revolutionary is one cutting food plants

indicators.note: a blade cutting something goes into the middle of it
a revolution turns something right round, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one
scran is British slang for food

explanation.surface: A rebel is the person slicing up food plants such as vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like the subject of the sentence, but it reverses the whole assembled string, not just one word. Scran is informal British, especially northern, slang for food.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcissi is the plural of narcissus, the genus of bulb plants that includes daffodils.

clue.text: Wrapping ground pepper with care

indicators.note: something ground is crushed to bits, so the letters are broken up and remade

blocks.note: taken as written, to be mixed
taken as written, to be mixed

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction: wrap the dish and grind pepper over it carefully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground pepper' reads as a spice; 'ground' is the signal and both the pepper and the care go into the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Crepe paper is a crinkled tissue used for decorations and as wrapping material for gifts and flowers.

clue.text: Kuwait’s capital Arabs are changing old settlement

indicators.note: the capital of a word is its capital letter, its head
letters that are changing take a new order

blocks.note: the first letter of the country's name
taken as written, to be mixed

explanation.surface: Arabs in Kuwait City are reshaping an ancient town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kuwait's capital' asks for a city, but the capital here is the opening letter. Skara Brae is a Neolithic stone village in Orkney, off northern Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Skara Brae is a remarkably preserved prehistoric village around five thousand years old, so it is a settlement of great age.

clue.text: Host’s mooring on island

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece set on another sits above it

blocks.note: an anchor moors a boat
the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A host describes their boat's mooring on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Man is the crossword favourite island, the Isle of Man between Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchorman presents and holds together a news or television broadcast, acting as its host.

clue.text: Port’s initially like Erith but without river

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter is kept
without means lacking, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: the first letter of the word
Erith is a town on the Thames in south-east London
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A port is said to be much like Erith, only without the river.
explanation.walkthrough: Erith is a Thames-side town in south-east London; drop its R and put the L in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Leith is the historic harbour district of Edinburgh on the Firth of Forth, a long-established Scottish seaport.

clue.text: Decapitated poet’s killers

indicators.note: losing the head means losing the first letter

blocks.note: Federico García Lorca was a Spanish poet, plus the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: The killers of a poet who was beheaded.
explanation.walkthrough: The poet is Lorca, who was in fact killed in the Spanish Civil War; his head letter goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Orcas are known as killer whales, so crosswords can call them simply killers.

clue.text: Rambling on downs and upland

indicators.note: rambling wanders all over the place, so the letters stray from their order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be mixed

explanation.surface: Walkers out hiking over the downs and the hills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rambling' is perfect for the walking surface and also the mixing signal. Downs are rolling chalk hills in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Snowdon is the highest mountain in Wales, so it is a large piece of high ground.

clue.text: Firm in Russian city concerning for Scotland

blocks.note: Perm is a city in the Urals
anent is an old word for concerning, still used in Scots

explanation.surface: A company based in a Russian city with business concerning Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a company; it is the adjective. 'For Scotland' flags that the word for concerning is a Scots usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Something firm is fixed and settled, and a permanent arrangement is one not expected to change.

clue.text: Broadcasts invitation to cheer flyer

blocks.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it
'hip, hip' is the call that invites the 'hooray'

explanation.surface: A radio show calls on listeners to applaud a pilot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hip hip' is the lead-in that prompts a crowd to shout hooray.
explanation.definitionFit: An airship is a powered lighter-than-air craft such as a Zeppelin, something that flies through the sky.

clue.text: Corresponding material in rubbish promos is rejected

definitions.note: the answer is a noun; the definition is a noun phrase naming a substance that corresponds in form to another

indicators.note: in means inside, so the letters sit inside the run of words
something rejected is sent back, so it reads the other way

blocks.note: the final letter of the first word, all of the second, and the first letter of the third

explanation.surface: Matching publicity material dumped among the rubbish is thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run backwards from the I of 'is' through 'promos' to the H ending 'rubbish'.
explanation.definitionFit: An isomorph is a substance with the same crystal form as another, so it is matter that corresponds structurally.

clue.text: Get browned off about theatre that’s boring

indicators.note: about means surrounding on every side, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: to tan is to get browned, here by the sun; 'off' just completes the phrase browned off, meaning fed up
rep is short for repertory theatre

explanation.surface: Someone fed up with a dull theatre performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' looks like the dull show; it means drilling. A trepan is a surgical tool for boring holes in the skull.
explanation.definitionFit: A trepan is a cylindrical saw or drill used for cutting holes, so it is an instrument used for drilling.

clue.text: Body that’s downgraded parking on most of airport

indicators.note: most of something is all but a little, so the last letter is dropped
in a down clue, one piece set on another sits above it

blocks.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
Luton is an airport north of London

explanation.surface: An airport authority downgrades the parking at most of its site.
explanation.walkthrough: Luton is one of London's airports; its last letter goes and the parking letter sits on top.
explanation.definitionFit: In 2006 astronomers reclassified Pluto from planet to dwarf planet, so it is the celestial object that was demoted.

clue.text: I am cut by the heartless couple

indicators.note: without a heart, a word loses its middle letter
a word cut by something is split open with that thing in the gap

blocks.note: I'm is the contraction of I am
taken as written, before its middle goes

explanation.surface: A cold, heartless pair have snubbed me.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' acts on the word right after it, not on the couple, and 'cut by' means the contraction is split open to take the shortened word.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people in a romantic relationship are informally called an item, the same as a couple.

clue.text: It turned dark, turning fearful

indicators.note: something turned round faces the other way, so it reads backwards
turning about sends a word back on itself

blocks.note: taken as written
dim means dark

explanation.surface: Night fell and somebody grew frightened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It turned dark' reads as nightfall, but both turning words apply to the piece just before them.
explanation.definitionFit: A timid person lacks courage and is easily frightened, so the two adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Transported cup at Holi for aromatic oil

indicators.note: things transported are carried off and moved about, so the letters shift

blocks.note: taken as written, to be mixed

explanation.surface: A cup carried around at Holi, the Hindu festival of colours, for scented oil.
explanation.walkthrough: Holi is the Hindu spring festival of colours, which fits a South Asian fragrance; the words are only letters to shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Patchouli is a heavy fragrant essential oil from an Asian plant of the mint family, used in perfumes.

clue.text: Problem with sister getting in fake spirit

indicators.note: someone getting in goes inside, so one piece enters another

blocks.note: a nun is a religious sister
cod is British slang for fake or mock, as in cod Latin
rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: A problem with a sister who is drinking counterfeit liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: The tempting CON for 'fake' leaves no way to place the sister; the fake word needed is COD, a British usage meaning sham.
explanation.definitionFit: A conundrum is a puzzling question or difficult dilemma, which is a kind of problem.

clue.text: Short TV feature about northern tip

indicators.note: about means surrounding on every side, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: prog is short for programme
N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: A brief television segment about a northern headland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' shortens programme to the informal PROG rather than describing a brief show.
explanation.definitionFit: A prong is a pointed projection such as a fork's tine, and the pointed end of something is its tip.
